article_title: Sock sensors and smart mattresses - is this the future of dementia care?

tasks.prompt: What is the main hope behind the NHS-linked technology trial in Jyoti and Bharat Patel's home?
options: To detect changing needs early so people with dementia can live safely and independently at home longer
To replace every doctor with a smart mattress
To record all conversations for researchers
To train former magicians as nurses
tasks.correct_answer: To detect changing needs early so people with dementia can live safely and independently at home longer
tasks.explanation_hebrew: מטרת הניסוי היא לזהות סימנים מוקדמים לצורכי טיפול ולסייע לאנשים להישאר עצמאיים ובטוחים בבית.

tasks.prompt: What first made Bharat suspect that something was wrong with Jyoti?
options: She refused to use a smartwatch
She made unusual mistakes while setting up their stage act
She stopped eating tinned food
She fell after leaving their home at night
tasks.correct_answer: She made unusual mistakes while setting up their stage act
tasks.explanation_hebrew: בהופעות הקסמים הוא שם לב לטעויות לא אופייניות בהכנת הבמה.

tasks.prompt: In the article, what does “gait” mean when the smart socks and watch track long-term changes?
options: The couple's kitchen routine
The speed of internet data
The way someone walks
The family's spending on care
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הליכה או צורת ההליכה היא המשמעות של gait, ושינויים בה עשויים להעיד על שבריריות.

tasks.prompt: What does “earlier intervention” mean in Sarah Daniels's explanation of the sensors?
options: Waiting for a serious crisis before calling anyone
Removing all sensors once a problem starts
Moving everyone to a care home immediately
Providing support sooner when warning signs appear
tasks.correct_answer: Providing support sooner when warning signs appear
tasks.explanation_hebrew: התערבות מוקדמת היא מתן מענה לפני שהבעיה הופכת למשבר.

tasks.prompt: Which device is described as tracking Jyoti's heart and breathing rates during sleep?
options: A smart mattress
A sensor on the front door
A kitchen appliance sensor
A camera in the bedroom
tasks.explanation_hebrew: המזרן החכם עוקב אחרי השינה, הדופק והנשימה.

tasks.prompt: In the sentence about a wider “roll out”, what does that phrase mean?
options: Shutting the trial down after one week
Extending the technology to more users across the health service
Moving the smart beds outside the house
Publishing an audio recording of the family
tasks.correct_answer: Extending the technology to more users across the health service
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הביטוי מתייחס להרחבת השימוש בטכנולוגיה מעבר למשפחות המשתתפות בניסוי.

tasks.prompt: Describe two kinds of information collected by sensors in the Patels' home and what they may help detect.
expected_points: Door sensors can signal someone leaving at night
Movement sensors can indicate a fall
Kitchen sensors can show whether Jyoti has eaten or followed her routine
The mattress monitors sleep, heart rate and breathing for possible infection signs
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לציין שני מכשירים והקשר הטיפולי שלהם; אין לטעון שמדובר במצלמות או בהקלטת קול.

tasks.prompt: Why might some families hesitate to use this technology even though the devices do not record sound or video?
expected_points: Sensors still collect considerable information about daily habits
Clinical staff remotely access and analyse the data
Some people may feel uneasy about privacy despite the absence of audio or video
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להבחין בין חשש מגישה לנתונים לבין טענה שגויה שהמכשירים מצלמים או מקליטים.

tasks.prompt: Summarise the Patels' experience and the trial's possible benefits and trade-offs.
expected_points: Jyoti was diagnosed with Alzheimer's and the couple joined the UK DRI trial
Home sensors and a smart mattress monitor routines and signs of changing health
Early signals may support timely care and longer independence at home
Monitoring is expected to cost about £2,000 per year
Privacy concerns remain, though the devices do not record sound or video
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לכתוב סיכום באנגלית המציג את סיפור המשפחה ואת היתרונות והמחיר או סוגיית הפרטיות, בלי לקבוע שהניסוי כבר הוכח כמוצלח.

tasks.prompt: Using details from the article, explain whether the trial's potential for preventing a crisis could justify its cost and data collection.
expected_points: The clinical team hopes to spot infection, falls or disruption to routine early
Bharat reports greater peace of mind
Annual cost is expected to be about £2,000, mostly monitoring and staff analysis
Daniels compares that cost with a couple of weeks in a care home
No sound or video is recorded but detailed behavioural data raises privacy questions
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לנמק באנגלית עמדה מאוזנת עם לפחות שתי ראיות מן הכתבה ולהבחין בין תקוות הניסוי לתוצאה שהוכחה בפועל.
